cards.name: Crisp
cards.summary: Sets the anti-aliasing of the selected type layer to Crisp: glyph edges get a moderate amount of partial pixels, so text looks a little sharper and more defined than Smooth without the jagged edge of None. Applies to the whole text layer (harvest: antiAliasNone -> antiAliasCrisp). Needs a text layer selected.
use_for: small-to-medium UI and website text in screen mockups where Smooth looks soft
captions and body copy on social graphics exported at screen resolution
avoid: large display headlines: the difference between methods is invisible; Smooth is fine
pixel-art or bitmap-style lettering that must stay hard-edged: use None

cards.name: None

use_for: pixel-art and retro 8-bit game lettering
text that will become a hard-edged mask or selection

avoid: normal headlines and body copy: the jagged edges look broken; use Sharp, Crisp, Strong or Smooth

cards.name: Convert Text Shape Type
cards.summary: Toggles the selected type layer between point text and paragraph (box) text. The menu label is state dependent: the harvest read Convert Text Shape Type in its no-document walk and Convert to Paragraph Text in its audit walk, and the live run on the text fixture was recorded in History as Convert to Paragraph Text (point text became paragraph text). Point text becomes a text box whose lines wrap; paragraph text becomes point text with a hard return at the end of each line, and characters hidden by box overflow are dropped.
